name: Discussion for truth (vāda)
method_summary: Examining a question with a partner by thesis and counter-thesis, proving and refuting only with the means of knowledge and tarka, within accepted tenets, in the five-membered form, aiming at ascertainment rather than victory.
prerequisites: knowledge of the means of knowledge and of the members

name: Wrangling and cavilling to protect truth
method_summary: Using contentious debate — including quibbles and futile rejoinders, or pure refutation without a counter-thesis — only to protect an ascertained truth from opponents, as a fence of thorny branches protects seedlings.

warnings.text: Quibbles, futile rejoinders and points of defeat are defined so that they can be avoided in one's own speech and exposed in the opponent's (NBh 1.1.1); vitaṇḍā without any purpose collapses into prattle.

name: Repeated study of the science of the self
method_summary: Study and retention of the science of the self, practised constantly as study, listening and reflection.

name: Discussion with the learned (saṃvāda)
method_summary: Discussion with pupils, teachers, fellow-students and distinguished seekers of the good who are free of envy — even without advancing one's own counter-thesis — for the ripening of wisdom: cutting doubt, understanding the unknown, confirming what has been ascertained.

name: Yoga and the practice of samādhi (Nyāya)
method_summary: Repeated practice of a particular samādhi as the means to knowledge of truth, in solitary places such as forests, caves and sandbanks, with the method of the inner self learned from the Yoga śāstra — austerity, breath-control, sense-withdrawal, meditation and fixation — and repeated contemplation of sense-objects to abandon attachment and aversion.
stage: after purification by yama and niyama

warnings.text: Objects intrude by their force and hunger and the like drive one away from samādhi; its arising depends on the continuing effect of previous practice.

equivalents.note: Vātsyāyana refers the method to the Yoga śāstra and names limbs of it; Nyāya's aim is knowledge of the self as distinct, not the Yoga's isolation of puruṣa.

name: Purification of the self by restraints and observances
method_summary: Yama — the means of dharma common to all life-stages — and niyama — the particular observances — purify the self by removing demerit and increasing merit, as preparation for liberation.

equivalents.note: Nyāya takes over the pair from the Yoga śāstra without listing its members.

name: Cultivating the notion of the unlovely (aśubhasaṃjñā)
method_summary: Against the passion-producing notion of a body as a beautiful whole ('woman', 'man', with its attractive details), one cultivates the notion of its parts — hair, body-hair, flesh, blood, bone, sinew, veins, phlegm, bile, excrement and so on; as this is cultivated, lustful passion is abandoned.

equivalents.note: Buddhist contemplation of the unattractive (e.g. the parts of the body); similar content, different doctrinal frame (Nyāya affirms the self).

name: Repeated contemplation of objects and of the body (prasaṅkhyāna)
method_summary: First contemplating the objects of desire whose false construction breeds attachment, aversion and delusion, until that false construction ceases; then contemplating the body and the rest within, until the I-notion ceases; one who dwells detached within and without is called liberated.

name: Reflection (manana) by reasoning
method_summary: Examining by reasoning, after hearing scripture, what has been heard — above all about the Lord and the self; Udayana calls such reasoning itself a form of worship.

equivalents.note: Nyāya locates itself at the manana stage of the Upaniṣadic triad; its object (a self distinct from Īśvara and from other selves) differs from Advaita's.

name: Worship of the Lord (Nyāya)
method_summary: Worship (upāsti) of the Lord, declared by the wise to be the path to heaven and liberation; for the Naiyāyika it includes the reasoned contemplation of Him.

name: Observances for the unseen (Vaiśeṣika)
method_summary: Ablution, fasting, celibacy, residence in the teacher's household, forest-dwelling, sacrifice, giving, sprinkling, and observances regarding directions, lunar mansions, mantras and times — undertaken for the unseen result (adṛṣṭa).

warnings.text: Fasting is listed without further prescription; no durations are given in the sūtra (prolonged fasting is not described here).

name: Pure food taken with restraint
method_summary: Eating food that is pure — of desirable colour, taste, smell and touch, sprinkled and consecrated, given by the untainted and taken with the proper recitation — together with self-restraint, since without restraint pure food yields no prosperity; taint lies in injury.

name: Giving (dāna) in Vaiśeṣika ethics
method_summary: Giving and receiving as deliberate acts yielding merit, with rules regarding recipients who are superior, equal or inferior in merit.

name: Yoga: the mind abiding in the self (Vaiśeṣika)
method_summary: Withdrawing the mind from contact with the senses so that it abides in the self, where the embodied one has neither pleasure nor pain; through a particular conjunction of self and mind the yogin perceives the self.
signs_of_progress: absence of pleasure and pain while embodied

name: Duties of the life-stages and common duties (Vaiśeṣika)
method_summary: Following the four life-stages with pure intention, and the common duties — faith, non-injury, benevolence, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy, purity of intention, freedom from anger, ablution, pure things, devotion to a chosen deity, fasting, heedfulness — besides particular duties of class and stage.
notes: The list of common duties is recalled with low confidence.
